text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"A meta-analysis of ten placebo-controlled trials found creatine improved memory overall in healthy adults (SMD = 0.29, 95% CI 0.04-0.53).","cited_pids":["0ad353ba1b7a#1","0ad353ba1b7a#2"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"The largest creatine memory effect in that meta-analysis was in adults aged 66-76 (SMD = 0.88).","cited_pids":["0ad353ba1b7a#1","0ad353ba1b7a#2"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"In that meta-analysis, creatine had no significant memory effect in younger adults aged 11-31.","cited_pids":["0ad353ba1b7a#1","0ad353ba1b7a#2"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"A separate summary describes creatine's effects on cognition as inconsistent in younger healthy populations.","cited_pids":["a87aba48cead#0"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"A randomised study reported only a small possible cognitive benefit of creatine and called for larger trials.","cited_pids":["345f16942ce0#2"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"A recent review said cognitive benefits of creatine are less firmly established than its benefits for muscle performance.","cited_pids":["7b1dc217a536#1"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"One trial labelled its cognitive and memory findings with creatine as exploratory.","cited_pids":["79a9a0887b76#2"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"A modest memory benefit of creatine in healthy adults is plausible, especially in older adults.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c9","text":"The evidence on creatine and memory is not conclusive for younger adults.","cited_pids":[]}]}
